rows.title: CT towns say they’re struggling with change to car tax law
rows.standfirst: Some CT towns have seen dips in their grand lists caused by changes to the state’s car tax law, which in turn have impacted their budgets.

rows.title: Lamont, legislators seek sweet-spot strategy as economy sours
rows.standfirst: Should CT use reserves to patch holes left by federal policy changes? Or should it bend its ‘fiscal guardrails’? Or both? The debate is on.

rows.title: Lamont tries to ease fears over federal aid cutbacks
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont said that while CT must brace for cuts in federal aid, the state is better prepared to manage the crisis than most others.

rows.title: Some CT legislators call for more taxes on rich. Will Lamont agree?
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont has refused to increase taxes on CT’s wealthiest. But many fear that his resolve could soon be tested as never before.

rows.title: CT Senate leaders offer new plan to tax rich to mitigate federal cuts
rows.standfirst: Boosting the two highest marginal rates on the CT income tax would affect couples earning more than $500,000 and singles over $250,000.

rows.title: CT could withhold driver’s licenses from tax delinquents
rows.standfirst: The measure is sparking pushback from some who say it unfairly targets the poor while CT treats wealthy delinquent taxpayers with kid gloves.

rows.title: Lawmakers to offer CT budget that pushes back on ‘fiscal guardrails’
rows.standfirst: State legislators will propose their budget Tuesday, using every loophole and maneuver available to bend budget caps without breaking them.

rows.title: Big demand for this CT ag grant, but no money for it next year
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont toured a farm to celebrate Earth Day and a grant program that illustrated the reach and limits of spending cap constraints.

rows.title: Legislative committee’s budget aids CT schools, social services, but exceeds cap
rows.standfirst: The Appropriations Committee’s budget would invest in K-12 schools, higher education and child care — but legally exceed the spending cap.

rows.title: Finance panel backs bill to shrink CT transportation debt
rows.standfirst: A key committee OK’d bills that would reduce CT transportation construction debt and phase out property taxes on vehicles — in the 2030s.

rows.title: Lawmakers challenge Lamont to tax rich to pay for child tax credit
rows.standfirst: The finance committee proposed a 1.75% surcharge on capital gains earnings on individuals making over $1 million and couples over $2 million.

rows.title: Lamont negotiates healthy raises for CT state troopers
rows.standfirst: The raises for CT state troopers could trigger similar raises for the rest of the unionized state workforce.

rows.title: AG says Lamont didn’t break law handling ARPA interest
rows.standfirst: But a GOP leader said Lamont’s administration still was wrong for not reporting these interest dollars to legislators for nearly three years.

rows.title: As CT budget work enters final phase, rhetoric heats up
rows.standfirst: With pressure on the spending cap and the threat of federal cuts, CT legislators are facing a tricky political mix as they craft a budget.

rows.title: CT headed for second-largest surplus in state history
rows.standfirst: CT is headed for its second-largest surplus ever, but it’s unclear if officials will tap the $2.3 billion windfall to cover federal aid cuts.
